title: Model Demo Interfaces — From a Function to a Shareable App

questions.question: The page already limits the text area with maxlength. Why does the server check the length again?
options: Browsers ignore maxlength on a text area unless JavaScript is turned off
Any client can send a request without the page
The browser applies maxlength only after the model call ends
The maxlength attribute counts bytes, so it allows too many characters
questions.explanation: A browser check helps honest users only. A script or curl can send any body, so the server repeats every check.

questions.question: What are the three parts of the demo contract in this lesson?
options: The prompt, the model weights, and the GPU server
The input, the model call, and the output
The frontend, the backend, and the database layer
The sign-in page, the payment page, and the result page
questions.explanation: The contract has an input, a model call, and an output. The demo puts a limit on each part, and errors are part of the output.

questions.question: Why does the demo page send a POST request and read the stream with fetch() instead of using EventSource?
options: EventSource cannot parse the text/event-stream format that the server returns
fetch() lowers the time to first token because it skips the response headers
A Python http.server handler can send a stream only in reply to a POST request
EventSource sends only GET requests, so the input goes into the URL
questions.explanation: EventSource only sends GET. A GET request carries the input in the URL, and servers and proxies write URLs to their access logs.

questions.question: What does the demo write to its request log?
options: The full request line with its query string and the raw client IP address
The route, status, latency, input length, and a keyed hash of the client
The stack trace of each failed request, with the file paths and the line numbers
The input text and the model reply, so that a reviewer can replay each request
questions.explanation: The log keeps no input text and no client address. The keyed hash counts requests per client without storing the address.

questions.question: The model fails after the server sent status 200 and three token events. What does the demo do?
options: It changes the status line to 500 and sends the response headers again
It runs the model again in the background and sends new tokens with no notice
It sends an error event in the stream, and the page shows it
It closes the connection with no message and lets the browser time out later
questions.explanation: The status line is already sent, so the server cannot change it. The stream carries an error event with a code, a message, and a hint.

questions.question: A hundred clients each stay under the per-client rate limit. Which control stops them from using the full model budget?
options: A smaller maxlength value on the text area of the HTML form on the page
A token bucket with a larger capacity and a faster refill for each client
A Content-Security-Policy header that allows only one hashed inline script
A daily usage cap that counts calls from all clients
questions.explanation: A rate limit controls each client but not the total. The usage cap counts every model call in a day and refuses calls after a fixed number.
